title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
hook: If the harness matters as much as the model, why is it still hand-written? JIT-Agent trains a model whose whole job is to synthesize a fresh harness for whatever task shows up.
key_points: Argues agent capability is split between the foundation model and the harness — memory, planning, action protocol, tool/skill orchestration.
Harness design today is manual and task-specific; the authors reframe it as a composable, machine-generatable artifact under a fixed four-module protocol.
JIT-Agent is trained to customize a harness per task, repair it when execution breaks, and self-evolve by distilling signals from an archive of past harnesses.
Reported gains: DeepSeek-V4-Flash passes GPT-5.6 on DeepSearchQA (+9.1) and OdysseyBench (+4.3); GLM-5.2 gains up to +20.2 points.
Generated harnesses are claimed competitive with mature runtimes like OpenCode and Claude Code, across DeepSeek V4, Mimo-V2.5, and Qwen3.6.
Framing: harness intelligence as a trainable, transferable axis of capability orthogonal to model scaling.
content_html: Most work on making agents better points at the model. This paper points at everything around it — the harness: how memory is managed, how the agent plans, what the action protocol looks like, how tools and skills get orchestrated. The authors argue that layer can matter more than the model underneath, and yet it's still built by hand, one task at a time.
extra_html:
JIT-Agent's move is to treat the harness as an artifact a model can write. The authors fix a four-module protocol so harnesses become composable and machine-generatable, then train a model to produce one on the fly for a given task, patch it when execution goes wrong, and improve over time by mining an archive of harnesses it has already tried.

The reported numbers are the authors' own: DeepSeek-V4-Flash equipped with JIT-Agent is said to overtake GPT-5.6 on DeepSearchQA (+9.1) and OdysseyBench (+4.3), with GLM-5.2 gaining up to +20.2 points, and generated harnesses landing competitive with hand-built runtimes such as OpenCode and Claude Code. Read those as claims pending replication; the more durable idea is the framing — harness intelligence as a dimension you can train and transfer, separate from scaling the model. See the arXiv preprint for the full protocol and evaluation setup.

related.title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable, Navigable, and Editable
related.hook: An agent is only as good as its harness — the code that builds prompts, manages state, calls tools. The real bottleneck isn't editing that code, it's finding where a behavior lives in a huge codebase.

related.title: Harness-1: RL for Search Agents with State-Externalizing Harnesses
related.hook: Stop making the policy remember everything. Harness-1 moves a search agent's bookkeeping into the environment, so RL only has to learn the decisions that matter.

related.title: Agentic Environment Engineering: A Survey
related.hook: Agents only get as good as the worlds they practice in. This survey maps the full lifecycle of agent environments — how we model, synthesize, evaluate, and grow them.

flashcards.prompt: What does JIT-Agent generate, and when?
flashcards.back_html: A task-adaptive agent harness — memory, planning, action protocol, tool/skill orchestration — synthesized just-in-time for whatever task an off-the-shelf agentic LLM is handed.

flashcards.prompt: What claim does the paper make about where agent capability comes from?

choices.text: The harness can dominate the foundation model's contribution, making it a separate axis of capability
The harness is a thin wrapper whose effect vanishes once the model is strong enough
Capability is determined almost entirely by pretraining data scale
Harness quality only matters for GUI agents, not text agents

flashcards.explanation_html: The authors frame harness intelligence as trainable, transferable, and orthogonal to model scaling — not a side-effect of model quality.

flashcards.prompt: Beyond generating a harness once, what two other abilities is JIT-Agent trained for?
flashcards.back_html: Repairing harnesses so execution stays stable and reliable, and self-evolving by distilling performance signals from a growing archive of prior harness configurations.
